newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urges action on campaign finance.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges action on campaign finance.

text.p: President Clinton urged Congress on Wednesday to enact campaign finance reform legislation, as hearings continued into questionable contributions during the 1996 campaign.

Clinton said in a statement issued by the White House that he supported efforts by Republican Sen. John McCain of Arizona and Democrat Sen. Russell Feingold of Wisconsin to bring a campaign finance reform bill to a vote in September.
"This year, we have an opportunity to come together across party lines to act and pass reform that cleans up the campaign finance system," Clinton said in a statement issued by the White House.
"We have an opportunity and an obligation to restore the trust of the American people in their politics -- and this is our chance to do it," he said.

Hearings continued Wednesday by the Senate Governmental Affairs Committee, which is investigating how foreign money, mostly from Asian business interests, illegally flowed into 1996 political campaigns and whether U.S. security was damaged or favours bought.

"The president believes that the public discussion of the shortcomings in the 1996 campaign have amply pointed out the need for campaign finance reform," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said in a news briefing. "And we ought to get on to that debate now, having clearly made plain that we need reform in the system."
